page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration within the cost-optimized E2 family, configured with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. The processing hardware consists of 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock of 2.2 GHz with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache architecture allocates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 55 MB L3 cache. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate performance tiers primarily restricted by clock frequency and core count. Synthetic CPU stress tests demonstrate lower-quartile execution, with stress-ng single-core recording 1106.18 and multi-core recording 2891.86. Geekbench testing yields 897.0 in single-core and 1973.0 in multi-core metrics, positioning integer, text, and image manipulation throughput in the bottom tier. In contrast, memory-centric metrics show moderate stability; the PassMark memory benchmark achieved an average score of 1969.62, supported by large-block read and write bandwidth rates of 24.7 GB/sec and 21.34 GB/sec respectively.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the e2-highmem-4 a cost-effective option for memory-bound tasks that do not demand extensive raw computation. With Redis SET throughput reaching 2.61 million operations per second, this instance profile serves effectively for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, light data preparation pipelines, and back-office administrative services requiring ample RAM headroom.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.2 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory. The instance features an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, offering substantial memory capacity relative to compute resources without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results place raw processor performance in lower tiers, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1973.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3564.93. Memory throughput remains balanced, evidenced by an average PassMark memory score of 1969.62 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 2.6 million operations per second. Consequently, e2-highmem-4 is tailored for memory-intensive workloads that tolerate moderate compute speeds, including distributed caching layers, relational databases, background batch processors, and memory-heavy web application middleware.
